decisions.reasoning: Two findings are failing before any processing attempt has been made. Finding "picture_area" shows the recorded picture is 1620×1080 inside a 1920×1080 file at offset +150+0 — there is padding that must be cropped before framing. Finding "subject_size" shows the subject's shoulders span 50 % of the canvas at p50 (p95 at 62 %), exceeding the 55 % size cap gate, and the solve indicates moving the head down to 0.413 to hold within cap. The fix.reframe strategy explicitly addresses both "picture_area" and "subject_size", it is cheap, and no attempts have been made yet so the retry budget is fully intact at 2. The two warnings — "distance_steady" (1.75× apparent size change) and "headroom" (crown outside picture on 76 % of frames) — are recorded-content limits that cannot be corrected by any allowed fixer and are noted for the report only. No verification has been run yet (latest_verification is null), so deliver is not available. If fix.reframe fails to bring subject_size within the 55 % cap or picture_area into compliance, the next step would be to assess whether process.standard can then be run, or if the budget is spent, reshoot would be required with guidance to stand 2–3 m from the camera and frame head to mid-thigh.

The fix.reframe has already been applied and all measurement findings are now in a passing or warning state. The current findings show: pose_coverage at 0.998 (gate ≥ 0.6, pass), one_subject at 0.999 (gate ≥ 0.95, pass), subject_size p50 0.442 / p95 0.548 (gate ≤ 0.55, pass), picture_area fills the file (pass), face_exposure at 1.059 gain inside the [0.8, 1.25] clamp (pass). The two warnings — distance_steady at 1.75× and headroom crown_cut on 76 % of frames — are recorded-content limits flagged as warnings, not gate failures; they cannot be fixed by any allowed strategy. No gate is currently failing, so there is no reason to pick a targeted processor. With 0 reprocesses used and a retry budget of 2, this is the right moment to run the standard first-attempt render (process.standard), which is the standard strategy for a first attempt and has no gate-failure prerequisite. The latest_verification is null, meaning no render has been attempted yet. If process.standard produces a render that fails a gate — most likely separation — the next step would be process.separation_targeted; if the budget is then exhausted without passing, the exit is reshoot.

The latest verification (attempt_1, process.standard) failed on two gates: head_spread at 0.029 against a ≤0.02 threshold, and head_drift at 5.3 px against a ≤4.0 px threshold. These failures originate from camera/tripod instability — the performer also walks toward or away from the camera (distance_steady warning: 1.75× apparent size change, threshold ≤1.35×), and the crown leaves the picture on 76% of frames (headroom finding). No allowed strategy in the profile addresses head_spread or head_drift: fix.reframe addresses picture_area and subject_size; process.separation_targeted addresses separation only; process.standard addresses nothing specifically. There is no fixer or processor that can stabilise a drifting camera or reconstruct a crown that was never recorded. The retry budget shows 0 reprocesses used against a budget of 2, but spending retries on strategies that don't address the failing gates would be dishonest. The correct exit is reshoot: the performer must lock the camera on a tripod with no auto-reframe or digital stabilisation (to fix head_spread and head_drift), must not move toward or away from the camera during the take (distance_steady), and must ensure 12% headroom so the crown stays in frame throughout.
